posts.heading: September 23, 2026
posts.text:
The station recorded 321 feeder visits and 23 species, against a seven-day average of 235 visits and 20 species. Carolina Chickadees, Northern Cardinals, and Tufted Titmice dominated both audio detections and visual counts. Tufted Titmice accounted for 155 confirmed visits, while the Carolina Wren showed a significant spike in morning vocalizations.

The Gray Catbird marked its sixth appearance in the last week and the Black-and-white Warbler recorded its only visit during this period. The Red-shouldered Hawk and Pileated Woodpecker were also present, though less frequently. No new audio-only species were detected, and the core group of nine species recorded every day this week remained consistent with their recent history.

Activity spanned the full daylight period, beginning with a Gray Catbird sighting 4 minutes before sunrise and ending with a Ruby-throated Hummingbird 12 minutes before sunset. A Tufted Titmouse was observed perching on the rim of a treat bowl.

posts.heading: September 22, 2026
posts.text:
The station saw 428 feeder visits, nearly double the average of the past week, making it the busiest day in the last seven. While the count of 21 species was slightly above the recent average, the drop in auditory detections to 251 reflects a quieter overall acoustic profile compared to the 296 average. Regulars such as Tufted Titmice, House Finches, and Northern Cardinals dominated the visual records, maintaining their consistent presence throughout the week.

Several species appeared for the first time this week or returned after an absence. A Cedar Waxwing visited, marking its return after seven days away, while a Brown-headed Cowbird and an Eastern Bluebird were recorded for the first time in the current seven-day window. Common Grackles and Song Sparrows also appeared, joining the station's list of observed species for the second time this week.

Eastern Phoebe, present in all but one of the last seven days, was not recorded today. A Northern Cardinal was seen six minutes after sunset.

posts.heading: September 21, 2026
posts.text: The station recorded 124 feeder visits, compared to the recent weekly average of 230. The species count dipped to 18 from the mean of 20. Tufted Titmice were the most frequent visitors, seen 64 times, with Carolina Chickadees and Northern Cardinals following at 14 and 11 visits respectively. American Crows, Carolina Wrens, and Northern Cardinals provided the bulk of vocal detections. The day concluded with a Tufted Titmouse visiting 21 minutes before sunset, following its arrival 12 minutes before sunrise.
